answer: The right defense turns identity into recurring, checkable work. Each key must be bound to a hardware root that enforces a per-device rate limit on the work it can sign, and the binding is recorded in the quill attestation log. Two keys sharing one root are detected through a fable collision and merged, while the plume quota is enforced before the signature exists. A farm then needs N distinct devices rather than N distinct strings, which is a procurement cost no script can pay.
